questions.stem: Black exhaust smoke from a diesel engine is most commonly caused by:
options: Overload or poor combustion
A frozen cooling system
Water in the lubricating oil
Burning lubricating oil
questions.explanation: Check load, air supply, fuel injectors, and propeller condition.

questions.stem: Persistent blue exhaust smoke typically indicates:
options: Normal operation when warm
Too much air in the cylinders
Water in the fuel or a cold start
Burning lubricating oil
questions.explanation: Worn rings or valve guides, or oil carry-over.

questions.stem: The first thing to check immediately after a diesel engine starts is:
options: Bilge level
Anchor light
Oil pressure
Radio volume
questions.explanation: Low oil pressure can destroy an engine in seconds.

questions.stem: If a crankcase explosion is suspected, you should:
options: Open the crankcase doors to look inside
Add water to the crankcase to cool it
Stop the engine; keep the crankcase shut until cool
Speed up the engine to clear the vapour
questions.explanation: Fresh air can feed a second, more violent explosion.

questions.stem: Which check belongs before starting a diesel engine?
options: Draining the coolant to check for rust
Oil level, coolant level and sea suction open
Painting any rusty spots on the engine
Switching off the bilge alarm so it does not sound
questions.explanation: Check oil, coolant, fuel and sea water supply before every start.

questions.stem: The high coolant temperature alarm sounds. A sensible first action is to:
options: Open the pressure cap at once to check the level
Reduce load, tell the master, and check the usual causes
Switch off the alarm and continue at the same engine speed
Increase engine speed to push more water through
questions.explanation: Reduce heat input, inform the master, then check the common causes. Never open a hot pressure cap.

questions.stem: Thin white smoke on a cold start that clears as the engine warms is:
options: A sign of a failed head gasket
Normal
A sign of an overloaded engine
A sign of a blocked air filter
questions.explanation: White smoke that persists after warm-up is a concern. A brief puff on a cold start is normal.

questions.stem: Engine running hours are recorded mainly so that:
options: Servicing is done on time and problems are noticed early
The crew can be paid for time spent in the engine room
The fuel supplier can bill the vessel for each hour it runs
The insurer can set the premium by hours run each year
questions.explanation: Oil, filter and other services are scheduled by running hours.

questions.stem: An engine turns over normally but will not start. Which is a likely cause?
options: A full oil sump slowing the crankshaft
No fuel reaching the injectors
A clean air filter letting in too much air
Coolant at the right level but too cold
questions.explanation: A cranking engine that won't fire is short of fuel, air or compression.
